name: 東龍 北白川本店 (Tonryu Kitashirakawa Honten)

claims.text: The 福仙楼そば is described as a 醤油味 (soy-sauce-seasoned) bowl; standard ramen shoyu tare is wheat-based.
All broths are animal-based (pork bone, chicken carcass, chicken-feet gelatin) and noodles are egg noodles, so the entire ramen line is cooked in shared animal-derived stock.

The bowls are seasoned with a salt (shio) tare rather than a soy-sauce tare, so wheat soy sauce is not the primary seasoning; however this is not a substitute for being gluten-free because the noodles are wheat.
No chemical seasonings are used (無化調); the broth is a clear chicken stock.
The bowls are offered in a soy-sauce (shoyu) or salt tare; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, and no wheat-free tare is mentioned.
The broth is made from rendered beef fat and the toppings are beef tendon and wagyu fat, so the entire kitchen workflow is meat-based.

name: つけめん 恵那く (Tsukemen Enaku)

claims.text: Tsukemen is built on house-made wheat noodles dipped in a wheat-seasoned pork-bone-and-fish broth; gluten is unavoidable and no gluten-free option or separate prep is indicated.
All bowls use pork-bone and fish broth with meat and egg toppings; there is no vegan or vegetarian preparation.
Tsukemen-only shop: homemade wheat noodles in a fish-and-pork-bone broth with wheat-based soy seasoning typical of the style. No gluten-free handling or separation is described.
Side dishes such as the butter rice are finished with a soy (shoyu) reduction; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. No tamari/GF soy is mentioned.
Broth is fish-and-pork-bone based with pork chashu toppings; no plant-based preparation exists, so cross-contact is inherent to the whole menu.
The chuka-soba uses wheat noodles in a soy-style broth; standard Japanese soy sauce and tare contain wheat. No wheat-free preparation is offered.
Wheat ramen noodles are the base of every bowl and the shoyu tare is wheat-based; a nine-seat single-counter kitchen means no separation from gluten.
The standard ramen uses a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare, which in Japanese ramen almost always contains wheat.
Broths are chicken-bone plus fish/seafood dashi (bonito), and bowls are topped with pork chashu; there is no plant-based broth on offer.

name: 夢は力なり (Yume wa Chikara Nari)

claims.text: The bowl is a soy (shoyu) tare-based Jiro ramen; Japanese soy sauce / shoyu tare is brewed with wheat in nearly all cases, so the broth seasoning itself contains gluten in addition to the wheat noodles.
All bowls are built on pork/pork-bone broth with pork chashu and egg; no plant-based broth or vegan option is offered, so there is no vegan-safe preparation to protect from cross-contact.
